items.title: Jon Hendricks interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 29, 2000 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: Earl Gray — oh I hate it when they do that, they put the milk in a glass.

ctx.x: Yeah. We’re going to take a little break here and we’ll get our tea. That’s amazing.

But it was just everyday life to us, that’s just what went on. And actually in a lot of ways it was much more picturesque than it is now because there were no illusions about it. Everybody knew what was happening. Now everything is dressed up under a façade and actually the same thing is happening. The gangsters are functioning and they’re functioning because the politicians are helping them, the judges are helping them, and it’s all hidden beneath some kind of mask. Earl Gray — oh I hate it when they do that,…
They should have the people that make this stuff up sit and do this. So they know the kind of thing they’re giving people to deal with.
